description: Returns a device's measured readings: window, pixels, safe-area insets, corner radii, size classes, the status bar, the app's top bar (navigationBar: UINavigationBar, or Material 3's TopAppBar), the bottom tab bar (tabBar: UITabBar, or Material 3's NavigationBar), content margin, reserved regions and fold, one reading per screen and rotation. Gives the current runtime's readings unless a runtime is named; narrow them by screen, orientation or rotation, which must agree when both are given (rotation 90 on a phone is landscape). A null value has its reason in the reading's `missing`, keyed by the field's dotted path, such as cornerRadii.measured.

device.description: A device id from list_devices, such as iphone-17 or pixel-8.

rotation.description: The device's rotation; 90 puts its top edge on the window's left.

runtime.description: A runtime build such as 24A434, or a version such as 27.2 or 16, written exactly as list_devices gives it (27.0, not 27). A version names the device's current build when it is the current version, else that version's newest release build. The device's current build when omitted.

screen.description: A foldable's pose: closed, open, half-open or tent; every other device has main only.

name: get_device

bar.description: A bar's top edge and height in window coordinates.

corners.description: Corner radii for the reading's orientation, with where they come from.

cutout.description: The cutout's kind, where a run recorded it: none, notch, island (Dynamic Island), strip (the iPhone Duo's camera strip), hole (a hole punch).

density.description: Android: dots per inch; dp = px × 160 ÷ density.

width.description: In the device's unit, in the display's natural orientation.

contentMargin.description: SwiftUI's contentMargins(for: .container) on the sides of a view that spans the window.

measured.description: SwiftUI's concentricCornerRadii for a view that fills the window; on iOS 18.6, the corners of the view behind a full-screen sheet.

profile.description: The display's corners from the simulator's device profile (iOS) or the emulator's display configuration (Android).

fold.description: The hinge across the screen: its axis, its frame (a band on iOS, a line on Android), the margins either side (iOS) and whether it separates the window.

date.description: The newest date of the runs the reading's values come from.

missing.description: The reason per field path that is null: not read on this device, runtime, pose or orientation, or why the platform has no such value.

navigationBar.description: iOS: UINavigationBar with an inline title and with a large title. Android: Material 3's TopAppBar inside the safe area as `inline`.

regions.description: Occlusion regions UIKit reports, and Android's display cutout.

rotation.description: Degrees from the display's natural orientation (iOS: UIKit's portrait). At 90 the device's top edge is on the window's left: UIKit's landscapeRight, Android's ROTATION_90.

safeAreaInsets.description: iOS: the window's safeAreaInsets. Android: WindowInsets.safeDrawing, the larger of the system bars and the display cutout per side.

screen.description: `main`, or a foldable's pose: closed, open, half-open, tent.

placement.description: top; hidden; left or right (a column in a side inset); navigation-bar (the time in the navigation bar's row).

bottom.description: The gap from the frame's bottom to the window's bottom edge.

sideGap.description: The smallest gap to a side edge with five tabs with long titles (iOS); the frame's gap on Android.

style.description: capsule (iOS 26 and later), bar (iOS 18, Android's NavigationBar), column (the iPhone Duo, in a side inset).

rect.description: A frame in the reading's window coordinates: origin at the window's top left, in the device's unit.

prerelease.description: A pre-release build; never a device's `current`.

sizeClass.description: UIKit's size classes on iOS; on Android the window size classes, V1 in `sizeClass` and V2 in `sizeClassV2`.

title: Get a device's readings
